subject: ela
intro: Digital tools help writers create, share, and publish their work. A word processor is a program on a computer or tablet that lets you type, fix spelling errors automatically, and format your writing. Writers can also share their work digitally by emailing it, posting it on a class website, or printing it out. Working with a partner on the same digital document is called collaborating. Learning to use these tools helps you become a more organized, efficient, and connected writer.

items.prompt: What is one advantage of writing on a computer instead of by hand? Give a specific example.

steps: Think about what computers can do that paper cannot.
One advantage: computers have spell-check, which automatically underlines misspelled words so you can fix them.
Another: you can delete and retype without crossing things out or erasing.
Example: If you accidentally type 'teh' instead of 'the,' the spell-checker will flag it with a red underline so you can correct it instantly.
solution.answer: One advantage is that computers have spell-check, which automatically marks misspelled words. For example, if you type 'teh' instead of 'the,' the red underline tells you to fix it right away.

items.prompt: A student wants to share her story with her classmates without printing it. Name TWO digital ways she could share her writing.

steps: Think about digital sharing tools.
Option 1: She could email the document to her classmates or teacher.
Option 2: She could post it on a class website, blog, or shared folder.
Option 3: Her teacher could use a program like Google Classroom where everyone can read each other's work.
solution.answer: She could email it to her classmates, or her teacher could post it on a class website or shared online folder so everyone can read it.

items.prompt: What does 'typing' mean as a writing skill, and why is it different from writing by hand?

steps: Typing means pressing keys on a keyboard to produce letters and words on a screen.
It is different from handwriting because: your fingers press keys instead of holding a pencil, the text appears on a screen, and it is often faster once you learn where the keys are.
Typed text is easier to edit (you can delete, copy, paste) than handwritten text.
solution.answer: Typing means pressing keyboard keys to produce letters on a screen. Unlike handwriting, typed text can be deleted, moved, and formatted easily, making revision faster and neater.

items.prompt: Two students are writing a story together on the same shared document on a classroom tablet. What is this type of writing called, and what is one advantage of doing it this way?

steps: Writing together on the same document is called collaborating (or collaborative writing).
Advantage: both students can add ideas, fix mistakes, and read each other's work at the same time, even if they are not sitting next to each other.
solution.answer: This is called collaborative writing. An advantage is that both students can contribute ideas and see each other's changes right away, making the story stronger.

items.prompt: A student finishes typing his report on a computer. He wants to publish it so others can read it. List THREE ways he could publish or share his work.

steps: Publishing means making the writing available for others to read.
Option 1: Print it out and put it on a classroom bulletin board.
Option 2: Email it to family members.
Option 3: Post it on the class or school website.
Option 4: Share it on a class blog or digital portfolio.
solution.answer: He could: (1) print it out and display it in the classroom, (2) email it to family and friends, or (3) post it on the class website or digital portfolio.

items.prompt: Name the computer tool that checks for misspelled words and explain how it helps a writer.
items.hint: Think about the colored line that appears under a word when it is spelled wrong.

steps: The tool is called spell-check.
It helps because it automatically identifies possible spelling errors so the writer can fix them before sharing the piece.
solution.answer: Spell-check is the tool that checks for misspelled words. It helps writers by flagging errors with a colored underline so they can be corrected quickly.

items.prompt: What is one advantage of using a digital document over paper when you need to revise your writing?
items.hint: Think about what happens when you want to remove a sentence or change a word.

steps: On paper, you have to cross out or erase, which can make the page messy.
On a digital document, you can delete, retype, or move sentences without any mess.
solution.answer: One advantage is that you can delete or change any sentence instantly without crossing things out or making the page messy.

items.prompt: A student is writing a report and her classmate wants to read it and suggest improvements. How can they do this using digital tools if they are at home?

steps: The student can share the document digitally — by emailing it or sharing a link so the classmate can open it at home.
The classmate can type comments or suggestions right in the document.
solution.answer: She can email the document or share a link to it so her classmate can open it, read it, and type suggestions directly in the shared document.

items.prompt: True or False: Digital tools can only be used for writing stories, not informational reports or opinion pieces. Explain your answer.
items.hint: Think about all the different kinds of writing you do in school.

steps: False. Digital tools like word processors can be used for any type of writing: stories, informational reports, opinion pieces, letters, and more.
solution.answer: False. Digital tools can be used for any type of writing, including informational reports, opinion pieces, narratives, letters, and more.

items.prompt: List TWO advantages of typing your writing on a computer compared to writing by hand.
items.hint: Think about how digital writing helps with editing, sharing, and neatness.

steps: Advantage 1: Typed writing can be edited easily — you can delete, add, or move text without making the page messy.
Advantage 2: Typed writing can be shared instantly with many people by email or on a class website.
solution.answer: (1) Typed writing can be edited easily without crossing things out. (2) Digital writing can be shared instantly with classmates, teachers, or family by email or on a class website.
